thread_text:
jordan: Quick RFC follow-up — we still need to land on where telemetry -> billing boundary lives for metering. Two options: 1) emit token-level events directly from runtime (high fidelity, heavy volume), 2) emit compact usage envelopes from runtime and expand/attributed in ingest (lighter runtime, heavier ingest). pros/cons below, please weigh in. :thinking:
priya: Option 1 gives us exact provenance for audits and makes later reconciles easier. downside is runtime throughput and egress cost spikes; also harder to change attribution logic later.
emily: Agreed on provenance, but we've seen spikes cause OOMs in the runtime's batching thread. Also scaling the kafka topic for token events is nontrivial.
sam: Option 2 is appealing operationally — runtime emits compact envelope: {model, tenant, tokens, fingerprint} and ingest enriches attribution. can change enrichment logic without touching runtime. sample envelope prototype: ```{"m":"gpt-optim","t":"acct_123","tk":42,"fp":"sha1..."}```
jordan: Right. Key tradeoffs I want to highlight: auditability vs mutability of attribution rules, cost at runtime vs complexity at ingest, and disaster recovery when we backfill attribution.
priya: For audits we could keep a short-lived token-level retention in a cheaper cold tier if needed — but that still increases storage/egress. How short is short? 7 days? 30?
emily: Another angle: split responsibilities by SLA — runtime guarantees per-request envelope within 50ms, but ingest owns final attribution and can emit a ledger event later. That means billing windows need reconciliation windows and a clear canonical finalizer.
sam: On reconciliation: if ingest changes attribution logic, we must surface diffs for billing ops. Could add an audit delta event: final_ledger_id -> list of source envelopes changed. That helps chargebacks.
jordan: To keep SDK/runtime simple, I'm leaning Option 2 with a strict fingerprinting contract and a compact token envelope. Requirements: 1) envelope must include a stable request fingerprint, 2) runtime should include minimal provenance (model version, sequence len bucket, token counts), 3) ingest must be able to rehydrate full token path for forensic only when requested (on-demand backfill).
priya: Sounds reasonable. Two operational questions: how do we version the envelope schema? and how do we tag envelopes when runtime falls back to cheaper quantized variants (need attribution to know unit price)?
emily: Versioning: include "schema_v" integer on envelope. Backward compat in ingest to skip unknown fields. For variant tagging add fields: variant_id and perf_tier.
sam: I'll spike a lightweight producer format and a kafka topic with 7-day retention for envelopes + 90-day storage for final ledger events. We can add an async backfill job to rehydrate token-level detail from traces if audit demand arises.
jordan: Action items: @sam prototype envelope + schema v1 by EOW, @priya define audit SLA (days of raw tokens kept) and ops playbook for backfills, @emily draft reconciliation API for finalizer diffs. I'll update the RFC doc with the chosen direction. :+1:
